metadata.title: HyBGRAG: Hybrid Retrieval-Augmented Generation on Textual and Relational Knowledge Bases

problem.statement: The paper addresses the challenge of effectively answering 'hybrid' questions that require a synergy of both textual and relational information from a semi-structured knowledge base (SKB), a task existing RAG and GRAG methods struggle with.
limitations_of_prior_work: Existing RAG or GRAG methods focus solely on retrieving either textual or relational information, limiting their applicability for hybrid questions.
Existing methods cannot effectively tackle Hybrid Question Answering (HQA) which requires a synergy between textual and relational retrieval.
In hybrid questions, the aspects required to retrieve different types of information may not be easily distinguishable by LLMs.
LLMs struggle to distinguish between the textual and relational aspects of a question on the first attempt, necessitating further refinements.
research_questions: RQ1. Effectiveness: How well does HYBGRAG perform in real-world benchmarks?
RQ2. Ablation Study: Are all the design choices in HYBGRAG necessary?
RQ3. Interpretability: How does HYBGRAG refine its question routing based on feedback?

method.name: HYBGRAG
method.key_idea: HYBGRAG handles hybrid questions with a retriever bank, which leverages both textual and relational information simultaneously, and performs self-reflection to iteratively improve its question routing based on feedback from a carefully designed critic module.

components.name: retriever bank
components.function: Composed of multiple retrieval modules and a router, it is responsible for selecting and using the appropriate retrieval module to retrieve references.

components.name: text retrieval module
components.function: Retrieves documents using vector similarity search (VSS) between the question and documents in the embedding space, typically used when no entities can be extracted by the hybrid module.

components.name: hybrid retrieval module
components.function: Takes identified topic entities and useful relations as input, uses a graph retriever to extract entities in their ego-graph, and then ranks associated documents using VSS between the question and documents.

components.name: router
components.function: An LLM that performs question routing by identifying topic entities and useful relations, and then determines whether to use the text or hybrid retrieval module.

components.name: critic module
components.function: Provides feedback to help the router perform better question routing, divided into a validator and a commenter.

components.name: LLM validator (Cval)
components.function: Validates if the top retrieved references meet the requirements specified by the question, performing a binary classification task using reasoning paths as validation context.

components.name: LLM commenter (Ccom)
components.function: Provides corrective feedback to the router to help refine question routing, leveraging in-context learning with pre-collected examples.

techniques.name: self-reflection
techniques.purpose: To iteratively improve the accuracy of question routing and retrieval.
techniques.details: The router refines its actions based on feedback from the critic module over multiple iterations.

techniques.name: question routing
techniques.purpose: To determine the optimal retrieval strategy (textual or hybrid) and identify relevant entities/relations.
techniques.details: An LLM router identifies topic entities and useful relations, then selects the appropriate retrieval module.

techniques.name: vector similarity search (VSS)
techniques.purpose: To retrieve and rank documents based on semantic similarity.
techniques.details: Used in the text retrieval module and as a ranker in the hybrid retrieval module for documents associated with extracted entities.

techniques.name: graph retriever
techniques.purpose: To extract relational information from the knowledge graph.
techniques.details: Extracts entities within the ego-graph of identified topic entities, connected by useful relations.

techniques.name: few-shot examples
techniques.purpose: To guide the LLM router in identifying relational aspects.
techniques.details: Used by the router to identify topic entities and useful relations based on entity and relation types.

techniques.name: divide-and-conquer
techniques.purpose: To improve the performance and leverage pre-trained LLMs for the critic module.
techniques.details: The critic module is split into an LLM validator and an LLM commenter, each with independent contexts.

techniques.name: in-context learning (ICL)
techniques.purpose: To enable the commenter to provide high-quality, sophisticated feedback.
techniques.details: The commenter uses a small number of successful experiences (approx. 30) as examples to generate corrective feedback.

corpus.name: semi-structured knowledge base (SKB) consisting of a knowledge graph (KG) and unstructured text documents

rag_system.retrieval_strategy: Iterative self-reflection based question routing with a hybrid retriever bank (textual and relational information)

generator.context_integration: Retrieved references are incorporated into the prompt for generation and validation, using Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting.

challenges_addressed: Hybrid Question Answering (HQA) requiring both textual and relational information
LLM's struggle to distinguish between textual and relational aspects of a question on the first attempt

settings: Using Claude 3 Sonnet as base LLM (default)
Using Claude 3 Haiku for model size comparison

main_findings.claim: achieves significant performance gains with an average relative improvement in Hit@1 of 51%
outperforms all baselines significantly on STARK-MAG
outperforms all baselines significantly on STARK-PRIME
achieves a relative improvement in Hit@1 of 47% on STARK-MAG
achieves a relative improvement in Hit@1 of 55% on STARK-PRIME
outperforms all baselines in end-to-end RAG on CRAG using Llama 3.1 70B
outperforms all baselines in end-to-end RAG on CRAG using Claude 3 Sonnet

ablation_insights.effect: Improves performance compared to without context.
ablation_insights.delta: HYBGRAG (w/ Context, ICL) Hit@1 of 0.6540 vs. Val. w/o Context Hit@1 of 0.6105 on STARK-MAG

ablation_insights.effect: Improves performance compared to few-shot examples.
ablation_insights.delta: HYBGRAG (w/ Context, ICL) Hit@1 of 0.6540 vs. Com. w/ 5-Shot Hit@1 of 0.6465 on STARK-MAG

ablation_insights.effect: Performance improves significantly with more iterations.
ablation_insights.delta: STARK-MAG Hit@1 improves from ~0.45 (1 iteration) to ~0.65 (4 iterations); STARK-PRIME Hit@1 improves from ~0.15 (1 iteration) to ~0.28 (4 iterations)

ablation_insights.effect: Outperforms single-agent and no-agent baselines, highlighting the importance of self-reflection and effective feedback.
ablation_insights.delta: HYBGRAG (Multi-Agent) Hit@1 of 0.6540 vs. Router for SR (Single-Agent) Hit@1 of 0.6206 and Hybrid RM (No-Agent) Hit@1 of 0.5028 on STARK-MAG

efficiency_results.throughput: Claude 3 Haiku offers 1.96× speedup compared to Claude 3 Sonnet
efficiency_results.comparison: Hybrid retrieval module achieves 24% relative improvement in Hit@1 with only 2 API calls, and HYBGRAG achieves 51% with at most 14 API calls, both without training, compared to AVATAR requiring at least 500 API calls during training.

contributions.description: Proposes HYBGRAG, an agentic system that automatically refines question routing with self-reflection via a critic module.
Develops an adaptive framework that solves textual, relational, and hybrid questions using a unified retriever bank.
Demonstrates interpretability by justifying decision-making with an intuitive refinement path similar to Chain-of-Thought.
Achieves effectiveness by significantly outperforming all baselines on real-world Hybrid Question Answering (HQA) benchmarks.

comparisons.difference: Regular RAG focuses solely on retrieving textual information, overlooking interconnections between documents and failing to meet relational aspect requirements.
comparisons.evidence: Figure 1(a) and Table 1 show it misses relational aspects.

comparisons.difference: GRAG relies solely on relational information, misidentifying textual aspects as part of the relational one.
comparisons.evidence: Figure 1(b) and Table 1 show it misses textual aspects.

comparisons.difference: AVATAR proposes iterative prompt optimization via contrastive reasoning but may struggle to generate correct output on the first attempt, while HYBGRAG uses a carefully designed critic module for more effective feedback.
comparisons.evidence: HYBGRAG achieves 47.4% relative Hit@1 improvement over AVATAR on STARK-MAG and 54.9% on STARK-PRIME.

comparisons.difference: Existing self-reflective LLMs lack appropriate retrieval tools and guidance on how to refine retrieval effectively, and using pre-trained LLMs as critics without careful design results in suboptimal self-evaluation and overly implicit feedback.
comparisons.evidence: HYBGRAG outperforms Reflexion by a significant margin on STARK (e.g., 0.6540 Hit@1 vs 0.4071 on STARK-MAG).

comparisons.difference: The full HYBGRAG system significantly improves performance by tackling incorrect entity and relation extractions in the first iteration through its critic module, which the standalone Hybrid Retrieval Module lacks.
comparisons.evidence: HYBGRAG Hit@1 of 0.6540 vs. Hybrid Retrieval Module Hit@1 of 0.5028 on STARK-MAG.

comparisons.difference: The single-agent baseline relies on the router to make decisions and provide feedback, which generates plain text feedback that is less effective than HYBGRAG's carefully designed corrective feedback from a multi-agent critic module.
comparisons.evidence: HYBGRAG (Multi-Agent) Hit@1 of 0.6540 vs. Router for SR (Single-Agent) Hit@1 of 0.6206 on STARK-MAG.

limitations: HYBGRAG uses only the simplest retrieval modules, and various alternatives (e.g., cross-encoder ranker, PPR for hybrid retriever) are not explored.
HYBGRAG does not offer significant advantages in terms of domain adaptation, performing worse on STARK-PRIME (medicinal domain) than STARK-MAG (academic domain).
The commentator in HYBGRAG selects random experiences when performing In-Context Learning (ICL), which may not be optimal.
future_work: Exploring alternative retrieval modules, such as replacing the ranker with a cross-encoder ranker.
Using top-K entities from Personalized PageRank (PPR) as the retriever in the hybrid retrieval module.
Implementing a more sophisticated selection mechanism for ICL experiences in the commentator, e.g., selecting questions most relevant to the current one.
Further enhancing the capabilities of HYBGRAG to address current limitations.

key_terms.definition: A knowledge base where text documents are interconnected by relations, consisting of a knowledge graph (KG) and unstructured text documents associated with KG entities.
Questions that require both textual and relational information from a semi-structured knowledge base (SKB) to be answered correctly.
Given a SKB and a hybrid question, the task is to retrieve a set of documents where each document satisfies the requirements specified by both the relational and textual aspects of the question.
A component of HYBGRAG composed of multiple retrieval modules (text and hybrid) and a router, designed to handle diverse question types.
A component of HYBGRAG that provides feedback to the router to help refine question routing, consisting of an LLM validator and an LLM commenter.
An iterative process where HYBGRAG improves its question routing based on feedback from the critic module.
The process by which the LLM router determines the selection and usage of the appropriate retrieval module (text or hybrid) and identifies relevant topic entities and useful relations.
